# Agent documentation instructions

**Scope:** `.github/agents/docs/**`

Use the current
[AI Codebase Agency Policy](../../../.codex/CODEBASE_AGENCY_POLICY.md).
This directory's historical agent/Genesis documentation is not a repository-wide
permission grant or an automatic prohibition on authorized local work.

## Editing this documentation

- Read the current task and relevant source before editing.
- Preserve existing dirty work and explicit read-only/user boundaries.
- Document actual behavior, runtime capability and source dates. Distinguish
  implementation evidence from examples, proposed architecture and snapshots.
- Direct inspection/editing/testing is allowed. Delegation is optional when
  useful, available and authorized, not a prerequisite to reading agent files.
- Fix relevant documentation problems. Report other findings with evidence and
  owner/mitigation rather than imposing unlimited repository-wide repairs.
- Review according to risk; there is no fixed iteration count or universal
  public continuation/status-file requirement.

## Profiles, catalogs and authority

Markdown profile candidates, registry entries, nested YAML implementations,
templates and archived documents are different inventories. Do not infer
hosted activation from frontmatter, registry `status`, deprecation prose,
test fixtures or a body example. Preserve intentional profile tools/model
settings unless their change is explicitly authorized.

Old Pre-Genesis/SAFE_MODE states describe their dated autonomous subsystem;
they do not establish today's hosted Copilot capabilities. Actual GitHub
permissions, branches, reviews, environments, secrets and execution approvals
remain controls to verify for the relevant operation.

Authorized local/no-PR preparation is valid. Workflow publication/activation,
API writes, settings changes, approvals, merges and deployment require separate
operation-specific authorization. Keep owner/security reason guards and
self-healing execution approvals intact.

Use the requested response/session output for handoff. Archived instructions
remain historical references, not the “main” current instruction source.
